children: ADRs slid 5.7% at 10.20 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, caught in a broad retreat from AI hardware ahead of Nvidia's results. The drop sits awkwardly against TSMC's latest numbers. The foundry reported October revenue of about NT$586.9 billion, up 59.7% year over year and 14.7% from September.

The momentum runs through the year. January-to-October revenue reached NT$4,485.6 billion, up 43.3% from the same period of 2025, so October grew faster than the year-to-date pace. TSMC is also stepping into the Anthropic deal as a smaller cornerstone investor: the amended registration statement shows 6,756,756 Class N shares, about $500 million at the $74 midpoint. Stocktwits, in a report carried by Yahoo Finance, noted the overlap between Anthropic's investors, suppliers and customers.

That $500 million is roughly 0.03% of TSMC's $1.75 trillion market cap, so the stake is a relationship signal, not a financial driver. The real story is pricing power: monthly revenue growth near 60% while shares fall on sector fear. GuruFocus scores TSMC 98/100 on top-tier profitability, growth and balance sheet strength. At $384.59, ADRs sit within about 1% of the $382.65 GF Value, a fairly valued reading, which suggests the market is paying for the growth but not extrapolating it. The next measurable test is November revenue, due around December 10, which will show whether the October surge holds.

title: TSMC Stocks Slide 5.7% Despite October Sales Jumping 59.7% to a 2026 High
